title: Pilot gatewalkthrough & access verification - Cobalt HealthTech POC
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on verifying access, validating staging env connectivity, and triaging a latency regression seen in initial benchmarks. Agreed next steps: exchange infra diagram, run targeted 512-token perf test from Cobalt staging, Redwood to provide SOC2 + network checklist, schedule deeper security Q&A with infra and security owners.
action_items: Samir: Send updated infra diagram and minimal network checklist (includes port ranges and CIDR) - due 2026-04-04
Lena: Share lightweight perf script and expected baseline logs for 512-token test - due 2026-04-03
Priya (Cobalt): Confirm KMS provider and key rotation policy, share pointer to SOC2 report - due 2026-04-06
Ethan (Cobalt): Run the 10-run latency harness on staging and upload results to share link - due 2026-04-05
next_steps: Redwood to provision temporary dedicated test slot for 24h for Cobalt staging traffic (Samir to confirm window)
Customer to open firewall rule to allow Redwood egress IPs and confirm VPC peering attempt time
Schedule security deep dive with Redwood security SME week of 2026-04-07
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-02 15:00 PDT | Duration ~38m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Morris (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Chen (Cobalt Eng Mgr), Ethan Ruiz (Cobalt DevOps), Priya Rao (Cobalt Security), Leo Turner (Cobalt Product)

Auto-summary: Quick gatewalkthrough to verify access and run a short perf validation. Focus on the 30-40ms tail increase we saw in last run.

00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Samir from Redwood — we'll do a quick gatewalkthrough and confirm everyone has the right creds. Back of the room, Lena will cover the perf script and I'll run through the network checklist.
00:12 Maya: Thanks Samir, appreciate it. We've got Priya and Ethan on for security and infra. We'll keep it tight, we logged a regression yesterday in staging so want to get that triaged.
00:25 Lena: Hi all, quick note — the regression you're seeing, did you run the same token length distribution as our recommended baseline? sometimes small changes, uh, to prompt length will blow up the KV cache behavior.
00:40 Ethan: We ran the baseline from your repo, but we modified it to emulate user messages — longer context; could be that. The numbers: p95 moved from ~120ms to ~210ms when we scaled to 40 concurrent connections.
00:55 Samir: Ok, that profile helps. Two immediate checks: network path (VPC peering/egress) and warm cache behavior. Priya, any guardrails from security you want before we attempt peering?
01:10 Priya: Yes, we need the network diagram and proof of minimal access. Also we require keys to remain in our KMS. We don't want Redwood holding encryption keys — is that supported in the dedicated pilot?
01:25 Samir: Short answer: yes. For Dedicated and Private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. For this hosted POC slot, we can do a temporary KMS proxy but we'll make sure keys never leave your control in the dedicated flow. I'll add the details to the checklist.
01:40 Leo: Quick question on where the latency regression appears — is it on the inference node or in the routing layer?
01:52 Lena: From initial logs it looks like a mix. There's a small uptick in the token generation time per step under high concurrency, which suggests KV cache misses and batch timing. But also we saw a bit more jitter on the network path in the same window.
02:10 Samir: So two prongs: we run the short 512-token synthetic load with pinned model and no tool calls, measure raw token latency; and you run your end-to-end user flow. We'll compare.
02:25 Maya: Sounds good. Ethan can run the staging harness. Ethan?
02:30 Ethan: Yep, I can kick that off. One ask — can Redwood provide a stable egress IP range for the test so we can whitelist quickly?
02:42 Samir: Yes, I'll include the temp egress set in the checklist. It's a small CIDR list. Expect that in the doc I send.
02:50 Priya: Also, we need SOC two docs and evidence of SSO/SAML support for RBAC. Our procurement wants that before we move to production.
03:04 Samir: Understood. We have SOC2 Type II artifacts and SAML SSO; I'll attach them. Quick caveat: some of the private deployment work requires a separate agreement, but for the POC we can provide read-only artifacts and a security Q&A.
03:20 Lena: For the perf script, I'm going to share a lightweight python harness that hits the /generate endpoint with a 512-token static prompt and records per-token timings. It runs 10 iterations with increasing concurrency steps. That should highlight whether token-time is increasing because of batching strategy.
03:40 Ethan: Great. Do you have a baseline we should be comparing to?
03:45 Lena: Yes, we'll include the baseline numbers from our bench: median token time ~1.8ms on this model at seq=512 on the selected GPU, p95 ~3.5ms at low concurrency. But your environment will differ with network.
04:05 Maya: Also we have to confirm data retention — does Redwood store user messages for training by default? We need clear retention and opt-out.
04:18 Samir: Not by default for enterprise customers; hosted APIs are opt-in for research use, but business agreements can specify no retention or short retention windows. We'll document the policy in the security artifact bundle.
04:32 Priya: Good. Also, about VPC peering — we prefer a private gateway rather than peering, can Redwood support an AWS PrivateLink / interface?
04:45 Samir: Yes, PrivateLink is supported on Dedicated and Private. For hosted POC we can do an IP-based VPN or temporary peering. I'll propose the PrivateLink path in our follow-up but we can do the VPN for quick test.
05:02 Leo: On the product side — if the p95 is still high after tuning, what's the recommended next step? More caching or smaller batching?
05:12 Lena: It depends — if it's KV miss rate, we recommend prefix caching (pin hot contexts) and reduce batch window to favor latency. If it's network jitter, then move inference closer to the customer (dedicated pool in nearest region) or use our cached inference path.
05:30 Ethan: Are there any changes we need in our docker/gateway config for the sample harness? We run behind an nginx termination proxy.
05:40 Lena: Just ensure keepalive is enabled and your proxy doesn't buffer responses. Also set connection: close on the test harness to mimic mobile clients if you need. I'll include a minimal nginx snippet.
06:00 Samir: Ok let's move to verifying access — I have a checklist: 1) Service account created with API key, 2) Whitelist Redwood egress CIDRs, 3) Provide VPC peering info or VPN creds, 4) Identify KMS provider and confirm rotation policy. Do we have any blockers?
06:20 Maya: We have the service account sandbox created, but we haven't created the API key yet cause we wanted to confirm the egress CIDR.
06:30 Samir: No problem — I'll send the CIDR. Once you create the key we can provision the test slot.
06:40 Ethan: We can create the key after CIDR is confirmed. Also one little note: our staging cluster sits behind a NAT that multiplexes egress — might add a few extra ms. We'll annotate the test results to account for that.
07:00 Lena: Good call, annotate the topology in the logs. If you can, capture a traceroute; that'll help us see where the jitter comes from.
07:12 Priya: On identity — we use Okta for SAML, can Redwood map Okta groups to RBAC roles?
07:22 Samir: Yes, group mapping is supported. We'll include role mapping examples in the runbook.
07:35 Maya: Quick clarification — for the KMS proxy you mentioned, does that still allow us to rotate keys locally? We don't want Redwood to hold any static keys.
07:48 Samir: Correct — in the proxy model you retain control of keys; Redwood gets short-lived wrapped tokens. For Dedicated or Private, the key never leaves your KMS.
08:00 Leo: Are we likely to need Dedicated capacity for the desired latency SLO? We're aiming for sub-200ms p95 for typical user flows.
08:12 Lena: If you need consistent sub-200ms p95 at sustained QPS, Dedicated is the safer path since you get reserved GPU pools and less noisy neighbors. We can quantify with your traffic profile after the test runs.
08:30 Maya: Ok that's reasonable. Let's confirm the test results before we discuss budget.
08:40 Samir: Agreed. Next, I'm going to confirm the temporary test slot; Lena will share the perf harness by tomorrow. Priya you'll get SOC2 + KMS notes. Ethan you'll run the harness and upload results.
08:55 Ethan: One more ops question — what logging level do you need on our side? Do you want debug traces or just latency and error rates?
09:05 Lena: Start with latency, p50/p95/p99, and error counts. If those show issues, we'll ask for trace-level logs for a short window. Avoid debug for long periods due to noise.
09:20 Maya: Also please note our compliance team will want an NDA addendum around data flows for a POC. Is that typical?
09:30 Samir: Yes, we see that often. I'll loop in legal and attach a one-page addendum for POC data handling.
09:45 Leo: Anything else on the infra side?
09:50 Priya: One small ask — does Redwood keep audit logs per-token or at request granularity? We need per-request audit trail for compliance.
10:05 Samir: We provide request-level audit logs (request id, timestamp, model id, redacted prompt depending on retention). We'll outline fields in the artifact bundle.
10:20 Lena: Ok I'm going to drop the perf repo link in the follow-up and a quick usage readme. It contains the harness and a small helper to compute per-token timings.
10:35 Samir: Great. Before we wrap — quick recap of action items and owners: Samir sends infra diagram + egress CIDR + SOC2 pointer; Lena shares perf script; Ethan runs and uploads runs; Priya confirms KMS provider and rotation policy; schedule security deep dive next week. Anything to add?
10:55 Maya: No, that's it from engineering, thanks.
11:00 Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with the artifacts and proposed test window.
11:10 Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-words — e.g., KV cache appears in logs as "K V cash" in the auto-transcript, some product names tokenized oddly. Speaker overlap recorded once around 00:25.

Attachments referenced: perf-harness repo link (shared post-call), security-artefacts.zip (SOC2 pointer), infra-network-checklist.md (to be attached).

Explicit next steps (verbatim): Redwood to provision temporary dedicated test slot; customer to whitelist egress CIDRs and run 10-run 512-token test; Redwood to provide SOC2 + SAML examples by 2026-04-04.
